newsitem.title: SPAIN: FORECAST- Iberian bonds seen suffering Fed's blues.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST- Iberian bonds seen suffering Fed's blues.

text.p: Shrugging off an official rate cut in Spain and a prospective one in Portugal, Iberia's bond markets are likely to be depressed next week by fears of a Federal Reserve rate hike on March 25, analysts said on Friday.

The short end is expected to gain in Portugal as its central bank is seen following Spain's example on March 18 and lowering rates. The 10-year cash spread over Bunds is seen widening for both bonos and Portuguese bonds toward 140 and 120 basis points.
"The market is getting nervous about a possible rate hike in the U.S.," said Nuno Godihno, economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Lisbon.
Earlier on Friday, the Bank of Spain sanctioned its second rate cut of 1997, reducing key money rate by 25 basis points to 5.75.
That was after Thursday's annoucement of tame February CPI, which fell to a 2.5 percent rate year-on-year versus 2.9 percent increase in January and 3.2 percent in December.
But long-term bonos did not show enthusiasm at the news, with the 10-year future falling 37 basis points to 112.23 at around 1120 GMT, and the cash spread versus Bunds trading at around 129 bps.
"There's pressure at the international level. Debt markets are not looking at inflation news any more, especially at these good data," said Giovanni Polastri at 4CAST in London.
"On the horizon, there is still a possible delay in the whole EMU project. And that is taking a toll on the peripheral markets," he added.

As the recent EMU jitters started, the 10-year cash spread over Bunds has widened sharply from between 83 and 80 basis points when the euphoria over the two countries' chances of joining the single currency was at its height at the end of January.
"Longer term we remain positive, still expecting that the Iberian bond spread over Bunds should not be more than 100 or 110 basis points," said DMG's Gudinho.
After the official rate cut, Spain's yield curve was almost unmoved, with the three- to 10-year differential trading around 128 basis points from 129 at the close Thursday's evening.
"In the long term I expect the spread to widen, but I'd suggest buying if it breaks the 140 level for Spain," said Valentin Fernandez, economist at Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.
But until then the shorter maturities could offer a better deal.
"At this point I'd suggest buying something intermediate, switching in the five-year segment, for example the 7.9 February 2002 and selling three and 10-years," he added.
He was expecting a similar scenario for Portuguese bonds, after February inflation showed a modest rise of 0.2 percent from January to 2.9 percent year-on-year.
"The Bank of Portugal has room to cut rates," said Martin Amaral Neto at Banco Essi in Portugal.
After CPI, the long end was barely unchanged, with the 10-year spread versus Bunds trading around 110 basis points and the differential below Spain widened to minus 20 from minus 18.
Analysts expect a 20/25 basis point reduction in the 6.20 percent repo rate as soon as next Tuesday's operation.
"It's likely the Portuguese yield curve would steepen. But as time goes by, I'd suggest moving toward the five-year segment there as well," said Credit Lyonnais' Fernandez.
-- Madrid Newsroom, + 341 585 8340
